work_packages.spec:
GitHub builds for the new app, modelled on the old Sutra repo's workflows (READ-ONLY reference, never edit that repo: ~/Desktop/development/sutra/.github/workflows/test-native.yml, plugin-release-gate.yml, release-dmg.yml). The distribution is named sutra-pro with the console command sutra-pro (D88, D89; the chassis renames it before you start). Write:
1. .github/workflows/ci.yml: name ci; on push to main, pull_request and workflow_dispatch (input slow: boolean); top-level permissions contents read; concurrency group ci-${{ github.ref }} with cancel-in-progress; job test on a matrix of ubuntu-latest and macos-15; pinned major versions only: actions/checkout@v4, astral-sh/setup-uv@v5, actions/setup-node@v4 (node 20); uv venv .venv --python 3.11; uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -e ".[dev]"; scripts/py scripts/plan_tools.py check; scripts/gate.sh (the same gate as local merges: pytest and the node tests); with the slow input also SUTRA_SLOW=1 scripts/py -m pytest. Job package (ubuntu): uv build; scripts/py scripts/check_wheel.py dist/*.whl; install the wheel in a clean venv and run sutra-pro --help; upload dist as an artifact. Live, slow and browser suites never run by default.
2. .github/workflows/release-wheel.yml: on push of tags v* and workflow_dispatch (input tag); job guard (ubuntu, first): the tag must match [project].version of pyproject.toml via scripts/check_release_tag.py (accepts vX.Y.Z and vX.Y.Z-beta.N and compares X.Y.Z; beta suffix allowed; anything else exits 1 with an ::error:: line, like the old guard); job build: uv build, scripts/check_wheel.py, sha256 written per asset by the same job, upload with softprops/action-gh-release@v2 under the versioned wheel name plus a stable alias name sutra_pro-py3-none-any.whl, prerelease true for beta tags; job verify (ubuntu and macos): install the released wheel in a fresh venv and run sutra-pro --help.
3. scripts/check_release_tag.py: pure function check(tag, version) -> (ok, message) plus a CLI (exit 0 ok, 1 not); scripts/check_wheel.py: opens the wheel with zipfile and asserts that every glob of [tool.setuptools.package-data] in pyproject.toml matches at least one member whose source file exists in the tree, that entry_points.txt declares sutra-pro = sutra_app.__main__:main, and that METADATA Name is sutra-pro.
4. Tests (no network): tag guard cases (valid, beta, mismatch, wrong prefix, empty, v-less); the wheel checker against a wheel built in a tmp dir from a tiny fixture project and, when the build tooling exists, against the real project; workflow YAML structure with pyyaml (add it to the dev extra only if the chassis has not: check pyproject first and report a need otherwise): every workflow parses; every uses: is pinned to a version tag, never a branch; every workflow sets top-level permissions; ci.yml runs scripts/gate.sh; release-wheel.yml triggers on tags v* and its first job runs check_release_tag.py; no run: step echoes a secret.
5. docs/RELEASE.md: how to cut a release (bump version in pyproject, tag vX.Y.Z, push the tag), what each workflow does, asset names, the checks, how to install a release (uv tool install <wheel url>) and what is not built yet (the macOS app and DMG are REL-2; Windows only on request).

work_packages.spec: macOS app and DMG, modelled on the old repo's release-dmg.yml (READ-ONLY reference at ~/Desktop/development/sutra/.github/workflows/release-dmg.yml; never edit that repo). There is no desktop shell (D12), so the app is a thin bundle: Sutra Pro.app = launcher + bundled CPython + the wheel installed into the bundle. Write: scripts/build_macos_app.py (standard library only; flags --wheel, --arch arm64|x86_64, --out, --python-archive for offline use and tests; gets a python-build-standalone CPython 3.11 archive for the arch with a pinned checksum, cached; creates Contents/MacOS, Contents/Resources, Contents/Info.plist; installs the wheel with the bundled interpreter; writes the launcher; never signs); scripts/macos/launcher.sh (pick a free port 8780-8799 as sutra-pro does, SUTRA_DATA_DIR default ~/.sutra-pro, start the bundled python -m sutra_app --no-browser, wait for /api/health, open the default browser, stop the server when the app quits, log to ~/.sutra-pro/logs/app.log); scripts/macos/Info.plist.tmpl (CFBundleName Sutra Pro, a reverse-DNS identifier you decide and record in docs/notes/REL-2.md, version taken from the wheel); .github/workflows/release-macos.yml with jobs guard (tag must match pyproject via scripts/check_release_tag.py, first, on ubuntu), dmg (matrix arm64 on macos-15 and x86_64 on macos-15-intel, built natively; hdiutil create; ad-hoc codesign when the four APPLE_* secrets of the old workflow (APPLE_CERT_P12, APPLE_CERT_PASSWORD, APPLE_NOTARY_KEY, APPLE_NOTARY_KEY_ID/APPLE_NOTARY_ISSUER) are absent, Developer ID sign + notarize + staple when present; prove the bundle by running the bundled interpreter offline and requesting /api/health; stable asset names Sutra-Pro-<arch>.dmg plus a .sha256 written by the same leg), verify (both architectures must be on the release). Tests need no macOS tools: the bundle builder with a fake python archive and a fake wheel in tmp dirs, the Info.plist rendering, bash -n and quoting checks of the launcher, and workflow YAML structure (pinned actions, guard first, secrets only in the env of the signing steps). docs/RELEASE-macos.md holds the macOS section (docs/RELEASE.md belongs to REL-1).

work_packages.spec:
### GAP-OPS-1 Operator CLI, instance lock, logging, scripts (G03, G08, G09, G10, G11)
- **Owns (new).** `sutra_app/ops/__init__.py`, `sutra_app/ops/lock.py`, `sutra_app/ops/doctor.py`, `sutra_app/ops/logsetup.py`, `sutra_app/ops/cli.py`, `sutra_app/ops/envfile.py`, `sutra_app/ops/browser.py`, `scripts/run.sh`, `scripts/stop.sh`, `tests/ops/test_lock.py`, `tests/ops/test_doctor.py`, `tests/ops/test_logsetup.py`, `tests/ops/test_cli.py`, `tests/ops/test_envfile.py`, `tests/ops/test_browser.py`, `docs/notes/GAP-OPS-1.md`.
- **Transfers (after ORCH-8 merges).** `sutra_app/__main__.py` and `sutra_app/main.py` (ORCH-8): `main()` becomes a thin dispatcher and `create_app` gains the lock and the logging call.
- **Spec.**
  1. **CLI.** `sutra-pro [serve] [flags]` is unchanged (no subcommand = serve; the macOS launcher and CI `--help` keep working). New subcommands, each with `--json` and exit codes 0 ok / 1 problem found / 2 usage: `doctor`, `status`, `stop`, `config show|set|init|sync-library`, `open`. `backup`, `restore`, `export`, `prune`, `usage` are registered by GAP-DATA through `cli.COMMANDS` (a dict filled lazily by `importlib.import_module("sutra_app.ops.<mod>").register(sub)` when the module exists), so this package does not depend on it.
  2. **Instance lock.** `lock.py`: `InstanceLock(data_dir)` holds `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` on `<data>/app.lock` and writes `{pid, port, started, version}` JSON into `<data>/app.pid` (same file name the macOS launcher already uses, so both agree; the launcher's check "pid port" becomes read-compatible by writing `"<pid> <port>"` as the first line). `serve` takes the lock before `create_app`; if held: print "Sutra Pro is already running on http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ (pid N)", open the browser on it (unless `--no-browser`) and exit 0. A stale pid file with no lock is replaced. `stop` reads `app.pid`, sends SIGTERM, waits up to 20 s for the lock to free (the app's own ladder takes 12 s at most), then reports; never SIGKILLs the server (a server killed hard is repaired by reconcile, but the CLI does not cause it).
  3. **Doctor.** `doctor` runs 14 checks and prints one line each with a fix hint: Python >= 3.11; data dir exists or can be created, writable, free space >= 1 GB, mode 0700; database opens and `user_version` is known (never newer than this build); `.env` present or absent, mode 0600 if present; `claude` on PATH, version against 2.1.308, signed in via `claude auth status` (no model call), login method `claude.ai` (an API-key login is refused, D34); `codex` the same (0.146.0, `codex login status`); `gh` and `gh auth status` (optional); Chrome found (`J2_CHROME`, the standard macOS paths) because Audit screenshots need it, else "Audit will judge from code only"; port range 8780 to 8799 has a free port; no second instance; seed library complete (G24); default browser is Chrome-based (G10); locked settings sane (`send_mode=live` needs `J2_SMTP_*` present). `--offline` skips the CLI and browser checks. It reuses `connectors.factory` status probes (`build_router(...).status()`) and `engine.paths` helpers; it starts no server.
  4. **First run.** `serve` with an empty data folder prints the doctor summary (failures only) before the URL, and the app's Home start page shows the existing X1 banner. Nothing is installed (D34).
  5. **Config.** `config show` prints the effective `Settings.public()` and the engine layers (defaults, global `engine.json`, department files) with the source of each value; secrets never printed. `config set <field> <value> [--dept D]` validates with `EngineSettings` and writes `engine.json` atomically (the only way to set locked fields). `config init` writes `<data>/.env` from a commented template (names: `J2_OVERRIDE_KEY`, `J2_SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD/FROM`, `SUTRA_*` as comments) with mode 0600 and a freshly generated override key if asked (`--generate-override-key`); it refuses to overwrite.
  6. **Browser.** `browser.py`: `open_url(url, prefer)`: on macOS `open -a "Google Chrome" url` when Chrome exists and `--browser` is `auto|chrome`; else `webbrowser`. `--browser default` and `SUTRA_BROWSER_APP` override. Decision D92.
  7. **Logging.** `logsetup.configure(settings)`: root logger `INFO`; `RotatingFileHandler(<data>/logs/server.log, 5 MB x 5)`; `RedactingFilter` applies `orchestrator.redact.Redactor` (token, override key, `.env` values, secret-named environment values) to the message and arguments; format `ts level logger request_id message`; uvicorn access log goes to the same file with the query string removed; a middleware sets `X-Request-Id` (12 hex) on every response and in a context variable the filter prints. Exceptions are logged with the traceback but redacted. `sutra-pro --verbose` sets DEBUG. Called once from `create_app` (transfer of `main.py`).
  8. **Scripts.** `scripts/run.sh` (checkout use, D12): finds `.venv` (creates it with `uv venv --python 3.11` and installs `-e ".[dev]"` if absent, prints what it does), runs `python -m sutra_app doctor --offline` then `python -m sutra_app "$@"`. `scripts/stop.sh`: `python -m sutra_app stop`.
- **Acceptance.** `scripts/py -m pytest tests/ops -q`; `scripts/py -m sutra_app doctor --offline --json`; `scripts/py -m sutra_app config init --help`; `sh scripts/run.sh --help`.
- **Depends on.** ORCH-8, CN-9, E4, E0, GAP-W1.

work_packages.title: Data lifecycle: backup, restore, pre-upgrade backup, export of chart and team deliverables, prune of bulky run files
work_packages.spec:
### GAP-DATA Backup, restore, export, retention (G13)
- **Owns (new).** `sutra_app/ops/backup.py`, `sutra_app/ops/retention.py`, `sutra_app/ops/exporter.py`, `tests/ops/test_backup.py`, `tests/ops/test_retention.py`, `tests/ops/test_exporter.py`, `docs/notes/GAP-DATA.md`.
- **Spec.** All commands register through GAP-OPS-1's `cli.COMMANDS`.
  1. `sutra-pro backup [--to DIR] [--no-runs]` writes `sutra-pro-backup-<UTC>.tar.gz` (default `<data>/backups/`, mode 0600): a consistent copy of `db.sqlite3` made with `sqlite3.Connection.backup()` (works while the server runs; WAL-safe), `departments/**` (without `run.stdout.log`/`run.stderr.log` older than 7 days), `library/`, `agents/`, `connectors/policy.json`, `engine.json`, never `.env`, `app.lock`, `app.pid` or `logs/` (an option `--include-env` is refused with a printed reason), and a `MANIFEST.json` (app version, `user_version`, file list with sha256, UTC time). Keeps the newest 7 automatic backups.
  2. `sutra-pro restore FILE` refuses while the instance lock is held, refuses a manifest whose `user_version` is newer than this build, verifies every sha256, restores into a staging folder, then swaps (the current folder is moved to `<data>.before-restore-<UTC>`, never deleted).
  3. **Automatic backup before an upgrade.** `ops.backup.before_upgrade(settings)` is called by `serve` before `create_app`: if `db.sqlite3` exists and its `PRAGMA user_version` is lower than the migrations of this build, a backup (database only) is written to `<data>/backups/pre-upgrade-v<old>-to-v<new>.sqlite3` first. Failure to back up stops the start with the doctor-style message.
  4. `sutra-pro export chart [--out FILE]` writes the head org chart and the change log as JSON (library `OrgChart` / `ChartChange` models, schema versions in the file); `sutra-pro export team <dept> [--out DIR]` copies the department's charter (`goal.json`), the last finished run's `site/`, `documents`, `summary.json` and the atom ledger rows of that department as JSONL; `export usage --csv`. Export is read-only.
  5. `sutra-pro prune [--older-than 90d] [--dry-run]` (dry run is the default; `--yes` applies): removes only bulky evidence of **finished** runs older than the age: screenshots, `trace.jsonl`, `events.jsonl` (after the task's `events_offset` equals its size), `run.std*.log`, old backups beyond 7. It never deletes `summary.json`, `goal.json`, site versions, documents, `chat.jsonl`, `calls.jsonl`, or any database row. The Atom log and the usage table are append-only (D60) and stay; `prune` prints their row counts and sizes and runs `VACUUM` only offline (lock check). Retention of database rows is explicitly **not** done in v1 (decision D93, section 6): the E7 golden run measures 31 atoms and 30 usage rows for a whole mock run, so the tables grow by about 100 KB per run.
- **Acceptance.** `scripts/py -m pytest tests/ops/test_backup.py tests/ops/test_retention.py tests/ops/test_exporter.py -q`. The backup test starts the real app (stub), runs the Brew Lab scenario, backs up while it is live, restores into a new folder, starts a second app on it and compares the chart, the graph, the chats and the atom log row by row.
- **Depends on.** GAP-OPS-1, ORCH-8, E3, GAP-E2E (harness).

work_packages.title: Offline demo: the chat agent works with --offline (decide, change and assign answered from the message) so a team can be created and run with no CLI
work_packages.spec:
GAP-DEMO Offline demo (found by the scheduler's own smoke run, 2026-11-04; not in the coverage critic's list).

PROBLEM. `sutra-pro --offline` starts and answers /api/health, but the first chat message ends with: "I can't reach Claude or Codex right now (no usable answer and no team to fall back on). Nothing was changed." (server log: "stage decide failed (attempts): keyword fallback"). The offline router is stub-only and the StubConnector answers a schema with example_from_schema(): a valid but meaningless object, so every stage of the chat agent (decide, change, assign, retry) fails its semantic checks and the keyword fallback has no team to route to. J2's own mock mode works offline end to end; the app's offline mode must too, so that the owner can try the whole app (graph, function nodes, atoms, a finished run) without any login, and so that the install smoke test is meaningful.

GOAL. With `--offline` (SUTRA_OFFLINE=1) a message such as "A website for my cafe" creates a team (a department in the one global chart), the engine runs J2's mock scenario, the graph shows the five function nodes with atoms, and the run ends Done. A second message about the same topic reuses the team; a message about something else adds another team. No model, no CLI, no network.

SPEC.
1. sutra_app/orchestrator/agent/demo.py: a reply book for every stage of the chat agent keyed by the call tag (function, stage). Read connectors/stub.py (ReplyBook, the `scripted` callable, the reply order) and orchestrator/agent/{agent,planner,prompts,replies}.py first. Replies are computed from the prompt text (the user's message and the chart digest the prompt carries), deterministic: decide = reuse a department of the digest when the message shares a keyword with its name or goal, otherwise add; change = a ChartChangeRequest adding ONE department under the root named from the message topic (2 to 4 words), built with the closed models of library L2 (library/org_chart.py, tests/library/factories_org.py); assign = one assignment whose goal is the message and whose target is the department the change added or the reused one; retry = the same as the stage it retries. Closed library models only; nothing invented.
2. Wiring: connectors/factory.build_router takes an optional `replybook`; orchestrator/wiring.py passes the demo book when settings.offline is true and only then (SUTRA_CONNECTOR=stub without offline, and every existing test, keep the plain stub). The engine's own calls keep the engine's mock mode (ScriptedPort); do not route them through this book.
3. Tests: unit tests that each stage reply validates against its reply class and that decide/change/assign agree with each other; a test that runs the real ChatAgent over the stub with the demo book for three messages (new team, same topic reuses, other topic adds); an integration test that builds create_app with offline settings over a temp data dir (the FakeLauncher is fine; if the real engine process is cheap enough use it with a short timeout), posts "A website for my cafe" through the HTTP API and asserts: a department node, its five function nodes with chat sessions, an assignment/task, the reply text in the Sutra chat, and no 'can't reach' message.
4. Notes (docs/notes/GAP-DEMO.md): what offline can and cannot do (stub usage rows with provider stub, no Claude or Codex, the Test and sign-in buttons refuse with the offline message).
Do not change any prompt, a reply class of the chat agent, or the engine. Keep the demo book small (under 250 lines).

(2) Chassis files (pyproject.toml, README.md, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/TRACEABILITY.md, docs/DECISIONS.md) are edited by the scheduler, not by you. (3) J2 prompts and route paths do not change; the prompt goldens and CT-1's route table stay green.

work_packages.spec:
GAP-TRACE The two deferred chassis documents: the design overview (docs/DESIGN.md) and the traceability matrix (docs/TRACEABILITY.md), with a generator and a test (scheduler's package; the coverage critic listed them under GAP-DOCS chassis edits).

1. docs/DESIGN.md (one page, at most 250 lines). Purpose; the five tiers of the architecture (Experience, Orchestration, Department runtime, Connector layer, server contents) each with the modules that implement it AS BUILT (read docs/notes/*.md and list sutra_app/); the owner rules (a new app with no relation to the old sutra-ui and the J2 prototype's design; ONE global org chart; five function nodes with goal, constraints, context and work atom with verify as the teeth; a connector layer with a Claude and a Codex connector, CLI first; everything in J2 present; local only; every decision documented), each with the decision numbers and the modules that implement it; the as-built deviations that matter (from the 'deviations' sections of the notes: 15 to 25 bullets, each naming its package); known limits (docs/design/gaps.md findings G18 to G27, the offline demo limits in docs/notes/GAP-DEMO.md); how to run (plain paths; mention README.md and the docs of GAP-DOCS only as plain text, they may not exist yet); the packages by section; the links to docs/design/{engine,connectors,library,orchestrator,ui}.md, settlements/, function-nodes.md, DECISIONS.md, BUILD-PLAN.md, gaps.md and j2-sync.md.
2. scripts/build_traceability.py reads docs/build-plan.json, docs/DECISIONS.md (every '## D<n>' heading), docs/notes/*.md, sutra_app/engine/features.py (FEATURES), the route table that the contract tests use (tests/contracts, CT-1), docs/diagram/decisions.json and docs/diagram/gen.py, and writes docs/design/traceability.json and docs/TRACEABILITY.md. Rows: (a) each owner rule -> decisions -> modules -> tests; (b) each of the seven draw.io steps -> module -> test (start from the table in docs/design/gaps.md section 4 and update it with the tests that exist now; later tests under tests/e2e/test_step* are referenced by pattern); (c) each of the 15 chips of the runtime strip -> module; (d) each of the 30 J2 endpoints -> handler -> golden test; (e) each D-number in DECISIONS.md -> the packages it touches -> status (implemented, documented only, rejected); (f) each work package -> its owned paths -> its notes file -> its merge commit (git log --grep). Deterministic and sorted. `--check` verifies that docs/design/traceability.json parses, that every path or test file it names exists, that every D-number in DECISIONS.md has a row, and prints the first 20 problems with exit 1. It must NOT require the committed file to equal a fresh run: later packages add files and decisions, and their merges must not fail because of this test.
3. tests/test_traceability.py runs the --check on the real repository and unit-tests the parsers on small fixtures (a decision heading, a notes file, a plan entry); a dead path in a fixture must be reported.
4. Write docs/TRACEABILITY.md from the generator; docs/DESIGN.md by hand from the notes and sections.
Do not edit anything else.
